documents.unit: Learning Design Center / University AI guidance
documents.title: AI Use Policy and Guidance
documents.stance_why: The guidance sets no default for student AI use. Academic use is "governed by USD's academic integrity expectations and any additional requirements established by the instructor or academic program", and faculty "should clearly communicate whether and how AI may be used". It offers no tiers or templates. Its concrete rules cover data, tools, accountability and disclosure for all users, so the instructor and program hold the decision on coursework.
documents.summary: University-wide guidance from the Learning Design Center for faculty, staff and students. It sets data-protection limits, names Gemini and NotebookLM as the preferred toolkit, requires users to stay accountable and to verify and disclose AI use, and sends coursework decisions to instructors and programs. It also covers research, copyright and licensed library resources, and says it will be updated.

units.why: The guidance says USD "will review and update this guidance as the technology and regulatory environment develop", a commitment that the policy is provisional, so it is a revisit-regularly policy (P54), addressed to the institution (admin) over time, informing rather than binding.
units.anchor: will review and update this guidance as the technology and regulatory environment develop
units.frag_start: The University of San Diego will

units.why: "USD supports the thoughtful, ethical, and responsible use of artificial intelligence in teaching, learning, research, scholarship, and administrative work" is a framework preamble stating purpose, scope and principles, so P56; it is generally permissive but sets no rule.
units.anchor: supports the thoughtful, ethical, and responsible use of artificial intelligence in teaching, learning, research

units.why: "AI use remains subject to all existing university policies and procedures" ties AI use to existing data, privacy, integrity and copyright rules, which is P77 (comply with existing law and policy) rather than P45, which treats AI as a collaborator.
units.anchor: AI use remains subject to all existing university policies and procedures

units.why: "Using AI does not replace or bypass established review and approval processes" says AI cannot be used to skip existing reviews. It is a compliance-with-existing-process rule (P77); P65 is institutional review of tools, which this is not.
units.anchor: Using AI does not replace or bypass established review and approval processes

units.why: "Materials requiring review by the Office of General Counsel must still receive that review" is a specific application of the existing-process rule, so P77 with modality must.
units.anchor: Materials requiring review by the Office of General Counsel must still receive that review

units.why: "Academic work remains subject to course, program, and academic integrity requirements" places student AI use under existing course and integrity rules without setting a stance, so P77 (existing policy governs) not P04, since it does not say who decides.
units.anchor: Academic work remains subject to course, program, and academic integrity requirements

units.why: "Public-facing and official university materials must follow existing approval processes" governs AI-assisted official communications, i.e. operations outside teaching, so P76 (administrative AI use), binding all users.
units.anchor: Public-facing and official university materials must follow existing approval processes

units.why: "AI-generated materials must be reviewed by a USD employee before they are used for university business" is a human-review rule for AI output in university operations. P76 fits (operational use); P48 is limited to course materials.
units.anchor: AI-generated materials must be reviewed by a USD employee before they are used
units.fit_note: Also a human-review requirement for AI output; not restricted to course materials.

units.why: "The person using AI remains responsible for the final work and for any decisions made using it" makes users own what they produce, which is P29 (own everything you submit), with "must" force since responsibility is stated as an obligation.
units.anchor: The person using AI remains responsible for the final work

units.why: "consider the type of information involved and whether the tool is approved for that use" tells users to check data type and tool approval before using AI. This protects data and prefers vetted tools (P50); P117 is choosing a tool for the task.
units.anchor: consider the type of information involved and whether the tool is approved for that use

units.why: "Information shared with an AI service may include prompts, uploaded files, personal identifiers, account information" explains what is exposed and that providers differ in retention and sharing, a data-protection fact under P50; it states no rule itself.
units.anchor: Information shared with an AI service may include prompts, uploaded files, personal identifiers, account information

units.why: "may use university information with an AI tool only when" the information is public or the tool is reviewed and approved is a conditional restriction on data entering AI tools, P50, binding faculty, staff and students.
units.anchor: may use university information with an AI tool only when

units.why: "Access to an approved tool does not mean that every type of information or every proposed use is permitted" limits what approval implies and tells users to check data allowances, so it stays within P50 (data protection and vetted tools).
units.anchor: Access to an approved tool does not mean that every type of information

units.why: "adopted Google's AI products, including Gemini and NotebookLM, as its preferred and recommended AI toolkit" names the university-approved tools users are pointed to, P92 (use university-licensed or approved tools) not P17, which is for one course.
units.anchor: adopted Google’s AI products, including Gemini and NotebookLM, as its preferred and recommended AI toolkit
units.frag_start: The University of San Diego has

units.why: "Gemini is the designated platform for approved uses involving non-public university information" fixes the one sanctioned platform for non-public data, so P92 (approved tools); stance is a restriction on where such data may go.
units.anchor: Gemini is the designated platform for approved uses involving non-public university information

units.why: "Gemini and NotebookLM may assist with tasks such as drafting, summarizing, comparing, organizing, and analyzing university materials" permits AI for university work tasks. This is administrative/operational use (P76), not student coursework.
units.anchor: Gemini and NotebookLM may assist with tasks such as drafting, summarizing, comparing, organizing, and analyzing

units.why: "Users must still verify the resulting content and follow all applicable review and approval requirements" requires checking AI output before use, so P31 (verify AI output).
units.anchor: Users must still verify the resulting content and follow all applicable review and approval requirements

units.why: "Public or unapproved AI tools may be used only with information that is appropriate for public disclosure" limits what may be put into unapproved tools, P50, a restriction.
units.anchor: Public or unapproved AI tools may be used only with information

units.why: "Do not enter, upload, or connect: Student names, identification numbers, grades, or educational records" followed by a list of data classes is an explicit ban on entering sensitive data into public tools. P50 (protect personal data); P49 is course materials only.
units.anchor: Do not enter, upload, or connect: Student names, identification numbers, grades, or educational records
units.fit_note: The list also bans personnel data, unpublished research data, university IP, internal communications, financial/legal information and USD systems.

units.why: "These restrictions also apply to connectors, browser extensions, plug-ins, custom assistants, and third-party services" extends the data rules to AI embedded in or connected to other software, setting scope, so P61 (define what the policy covers).
units.anchor: These restrictions also apply to connectors, browser extensions, plug-ins, custom assistants, and third-party services
units.fit_note: Also covers AI built into browsers and plug-ins (cf. P07) but only for the data-entry restriction.

units.why: "Treat anything entered into a public or unapproved AI tool as though it could become publicly accessible" is advice to assume no confidentiality; it is data protection, P50, with "should" force.
units.anchor: Treat anything entered into a public or unapproved AI tool as though it could

units.why: "Before using any AI service, review its current privacy, data-retention, model-training, security, and acceptable-use terms" tells users to assess a tool before use. P117 (evaluate a tool) fits best; P65 is institutional review.
units.anchor: review its current privacy, data-retention, model-training, security, and acceptable-use terms
units.fit_note: The evaluation concerns terms of service and data handling, not accuracy or fit to the task.

units.why: "You are fully responsible for work produced with the assistance of AI" states that users own AI-assisted work, so P29, as a must-style obligation.
units.anchor: You are fully responsible for work produced with the assistance of AI

units.why: "AI-generated content may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, fabricated, outdated" warns that output is often wrong, which is P31 (verify AI output; it is often wrong), stated as information.
units.anchor: AI-generated content may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, fabricated, outdated

units.why: "Verify factual claims, quotations, calculations, citations, and references" is a direct instruction to check AI output before using it, so P31 with "should".
units.anchor: Verify factual claims, quotations, calculations, citations, and references

units.why: "Review it for bias, harmful assumptions, and accessibility" asks users to screen AI output for bias and accessibility. P31 (critically evaluate) is the nearest type; P97 is accessibility of tools and materials generally.
units.anchor: Review it for bias, harmful assumptions, and accessibility
units.fit_note: Adds bias and accessibility screening beyond factual accuracy.

units.why: "Use AI to enhance—not replace—your thinking, expertise, learning, and decision-making" keeps the user as the primary thinker, P32, stated as "should".
units.anchor: Use AI to enhance—not replace—your thinking, expertise, learning, and decision-making

units.why: "Be transparent when AI makes a meaningful contribution to academic, research, scholarly, or university work" sets a disclosure duty with a materiality threshold, so P24 (disclose AI use); "when appropriate or required" makes it conditional.
units.anchor: Be transparent when AI makes a meaningful contribution to academic, research, scholarly, or university work

units.why: "Identify the AI tool used. Explain how it was used." lists what a disclosure should include (tool and manner of use), so P25 (cite the tool, prompt, output), though it does not require the prompt or output.
units.anchor: Identify the AI tool used. Explain how it was used.
units.fit_note: Requires tool and description of use, not the prompt or output.

units.why: "Follow the requirements established by the instructor, academic program, publisher, research sponsor, professional field, or responsible university office" hands disclosure and use rules to these local authorities. It is P04 (others set the rule).
units.anchor: Follow the requirements established by the instructor, academic program, publisher, research sponsor, professional field
units.fit_note: Delegation extends beyond instructors to programs, publishers, sponsors and offices.

units.why: "consider who may be helped, harmed, included, or excluded by the use of AI" asks the community to weigh benefits and harms of using AI in context, so P118 with "should" (encourages).
units.anchor: consider who may be helped, harmed, included, or excluded by the use of AI

units.why: "challenge biased outputs" is a call to push back on biased AI output, naming a bias concern, P53 (name bias and harms); the sentence also has respect-for-privacy and IP duties.
units.anchor: Respect privacy, consent, ownership, and intellectual property; challenge biased outputs
units.fit_note: Also asks users to respect privacy, consent, ownership and IP.

units.why: "avoid using AI to mislead, discriminate, manipulate, or misrepresent" is a general conduct ban on deceptive or discriminatory AI use, P74.
units.anchor: avoid using AI to mislead, discriminate, manipulate, or misrepresent
units.frag_start: and avoid using AI to mislead,

units.why: "governed by USD's academic integrity expectations and any additional requirements established by the instructor or academic program" gives the decision on student AI use to integrity rules plus instructor or program, i.e. P04 (instructors set the rule), the document's main stance mechanism.
units.anchor: any additional requirements established by the instructor or academic program
units.frag_start: The use of generative AI in
units.fit_note: Program-level setting is also named (cf. P85).

units.why: "Review the AI expectations for each course and assignment" tells students to find out and follow the applicable rules, which is P78, not P10 (asking when unsure).
units.anchor: Review the AI expectations for each course and assignment

units.why: "Ask the instructor when permitted uses are unclear" is the ask-before-using rule, P10, for students.
units.anchor: Ask the instructor when permitted uses are unclear

units.why: "Cite or disclose AI use when required" tells students to disclose AI use where a rule requires, P24, conditional on the instructor or program.
units.anchor: Cite or disclose AI use when required

units.why: "Avoid submitting AI-generated work as their own" tells students not to hand in AI output as theirs: P19 (do not have AI produce the work you submit), stated as "should not".
units.anchor: Avoid submitting AI-generated work as their own

units.why: "Ensure that AI does not replace the learning or skill development an assignment is intended to support" asks students not to let AI displace learning; it is closest to P32 (AI must not replace their thinking).
units.anchor: Ensure that AI does not replace the learning or skill development
units.fit_note: Framed as protecting the assignment's learning purpose (cf. P41) rather than the student as thinker.

units.why: "Faculty should clearly communicate whether and how AI may be used" requires instructors to state AI expectations to students, P09 (state expectations in syllabus or assignment), though it names no specific location.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly communicate whether and how AI may be used
units.fit_note: Does not name the syllabus specifically.

units.why: "explain how those expectations relate to the assignment's learning outcomes" ties AI rules to learning outcomes, which is P83 (align AI decisions with objectives).
units.anchor: explain how those expectations relate to the assignment’s learning outcomes

units.why: "The use of AI in research remains subject to applicable requirements related to" IRB, privacy, sponsors and IP governs AI in research and scholarship, P62.
units.anchor: The use of AI in research remains subject to applicable requirements
units.frag_start: The use of AI in research

units.why: "Researchers should confirm that the selected tool is approved for the data involved and consult the appropriate research or compliance office" is a research-specific duty to check tool approval; P62 fits as research use.
units.anchor: Researchers should confirm that the selected tool is approved for the data involved
units.fit_note: Researchers include faculty and students; also directs them to compliance offices.

units.why: "Uploading articles, books, images, course materials, or other protected content to an AI platform may violate copyright, intellectual property, or license requirements" warns against uploading protected course materials, P49; risk is stated as "may violate".
units.anchor: Uploading articles, books, images, course materials, or other protected content

units.why: "Many library databases and electronic resources are governed by agreements that restrict copying, automated analysis, text and data mining, or use with generative AI" explains licensing limits on AI use of library resources, P52.
units.anchor: agreements that restrict copying, automated analysis, text and data mining, or use with generative AI

units.why: "Confirm that the proposed use is permitted" and "Review the terms governing the source" instruct users to check licence terms before using licensed material with AI, P52.
units.anchor: Confirm that the proposed use is permitted.

units.why: "Ask your instructor about academic use" repeats the ask-when-unsure rule for the general "When in doubt" section, aimed at students; P10.
units.anchor: Ask your instructor about academic use

units.why: "Review the Approved AI Tools and Data Allowances" sends users to the approved list, so P92 (use or know the approved tools).
units.anchor: Approved AI Tools and Data Allowances

units.why: "Contact Copley Library about licensed resources, citation, copyright, or text and data mining" directs people to library staff for help, P72 (human help), though it is not limited to students.
units.anchor: Contact Copley Library about licensed resources, citation, copyright, or text and data mining
units.fit_note: Addressed to all users, not only students.

units.why: "Consult the appropriate research or compliance office about research-related uses" points to offices for research questions: P115 (point to further guidance).
units.anchor: Consult the appropriate research or compliance office about research-related uses

units.why: "Contact Information Technology Services about security, integrations, connectors, or tool approval" directs users to ITS, P115.
units.anchor: Contact Information Technology Services about security, integrations, connectors, or tool approval

documents.unit: Shiley-Marcos School of Engineering, MS Applied Artificial Intelligence
documents.title: MS in Applied Artificial Intelligence Graduate Student Handbook 2026-2027
documents.stance_why: The handbook's Generative AI Guidelines allow AI with conditions: students "must be transparent about your use and disclose any generated content", must verify output, and are "encouraged to use ChatGPT and similar programs as a tool to support your own learning" but "not as a replacement for independent research and analysis". No ban, tiers or hand-off to instructors appear.
documents.summary: Program handbook for the MS in Applied AI with three short Generative AI Guidelines: disclose AI-generated content through citation, check the output, and use AI to support learning rather than replace independent work. The rest of the handbook is general graduate policy; its academic integrity section does not mention AI.

units.why: "you must be transparent about your use and disclose any generated content" is a mandatory disclosure rule for ChatGPT and similar tools, P24 (disclose with each submission); the rest of the sentence names written assignments, papers and other communication, and citations/documentation as the means.
units.anchor: must be transparent about your use and disclose any generated content
units.policy: Students using ChatGPT and similar programs must be transparent about their use and disclose any generated content as being produced by an AI program, including in written assignments, research papers and other forms of communication, through citations and documentation.

units.why: The example note "Responses generated by ChatGPT, an AI language model developed by OpenAI" models a citation naming the tool and its developer, so P25 (cite the tool); it does not require prompt or output, hence fit_note.
units.anchor: Responses generated by ChatGPT, an AI language model developed by OpenAI
units.fit_note: An example citation wording naming tool and developer only, not prompt or output.

units.why: "You are responsible for critically evaluating the accuracy, reliability, and quality of any information generated" makes students check AI output, and "verifying it through additional sources if necessary" says how. P31.
units.anchor: responsible for critically evaluating the accuracy, reliability, and quality of any information generated
units.policy: Students are responsible for critically evaluating the accuracy, reliability, and quality of any information generated by ChatGPT and similar programs and verifying it through additional sources if necessary.

units.why: "You are encouraged to use ChatGPT and similar programs as a tool to support your own learning" welcomes AI use for learning, the default-permissive stance (P02), with "encouraged" signalling should.
units.anchor: encouraged to use ChatGPT and similar programs as a tool to support your own learning
units.fit_note: Encouragement is for supporting learning and critical thinking specifically.

units.why: "but not as a replacement for independent research and analysis" bars using AI instead of doing the research and analysis, keeping the student as the problem-solver: P32 (should not).
units.anchor: not as a replacement for independent research and analysis
units.frag_start: but not as a replacement for

units.why: "must be accompanied by the development of your critical thinking skills and an understanding of their limitations" requires that AI use go with skill-building and knowing AI limits. P32 is nearest; the limits part also touches P31.
units.anchor: must be accompanied by the development of your critical thinking skills
units.frag_start: The use of ChatGPT and similar programs
units.fit_note: Also requires understanding the tools' limitations (cf. P31).

notes: Both handbooks reproduce the same three Generative AI Guidelines; the integrity sections of both handbooks list academic dishonesty (unauthorized assistance, plagiarism) but never mention AI, so they were not coded as AI policies. Honor Code PDF was not in the collect list. Many LDC units are university-wide data and tool rules rather than coursework rules. Data-entry restrictions are held under P50; administrative AI use under P76.
